rho_reference.strongest_available_basis: All four curves are prime-order curves over prime fields with j not 0 or 1728 (validator check against the ICV1 strings), so Aut(E) = {+-1}: negation is the only automorphism fold and no Frobenius fold exists.
rho_reference.gae_band_row: icv1-fp20-tm327-45c21191: ic = srenew mean S over its 144 measured runs, rho = rho-neg mean S over the same 144 (target, round) pairs; every row in gae_band_by_row

caveats: P28 passes with caveats (VAL-20261029-4aed57): about one third of its 2.3% gain is the scalar-multiplication saving; the other two thirds come from srenew needing 4.4% fewer relations (203.3 vs 212.7, CI [0.916, 0.996]) and 4.3% fewer trials, which the protocol did not predict and for which no mechanism is stated; it sits about two standard errors from zero. The w = 1 upper bound is 0.9955 (0.9945 to 0.9965 across 11 validator bootstrap seeds).
Four sizes were each decided at 95% with no multiplicity correction, as frozen. P24 and P32 are null and not covered by this file.
Two fresh curves per size, 24 targets x 6 rounds; the intervals cover target-to-target variation over two curves, not a population of curves. No exponent claim.

The measuring binary (583e62f0, EKS, AMD) and the replay binary (bf5eec6d, local Intel container) differ; replay is cross-binary and cross-host, 1440/1440 identical per session. Neither is an independent implementation; the validator stdlib recompute and [d]G = Q checks on 2,880 records are the implementation-independent checks.
Counted unit only; wall times are L2 records but not analysed. The image binary does not emit the bitop/v1 work fields.
promotion_note: No evidence blocker known to the validator remains for the four rows. Promotion itself is the Coordinator decision; this file records evidence admissibility, not authorization.
